name: Multi-brand
summary: Customer screens for several brands, often on phones: sign-up, checkout, account. Components never change; brand primitives do.
description: Multi-brand is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Customer screens for several brands, often on phones: sign-up, checkout, account. Components never change; brand primitives do.

ai.use_when: Companies that sell to customers under several brands, or white-label products shown to their clients' customers: sign-up, checkout, account and product pages.
ai.avoid_when: A single product with one brand, where the brand layer is cost with no user; or tools staff use all day. Use Dense data for those.

scenarios.text: A customer signs up for a plan on the Birch site, then manages it in the shared account area.
A product team launches a fourth brand by adding brand primitives, without touching components.

summary.text: A plain shared voice. Each brand adds its own tone on top, never its own structure.

principles.text: Shared structure: object, state, next step.
Brand tone lives in headlines and marketing copy, not in errors.
Errors and confirmations read the same in every brand.
A button label stays on one line: it never breaks onto two.

out.why: Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not conversation. It admits only families in its roles. Its only messages go to support through a textarea.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not conversation. It admits only families in its roles. Its only messages go to support through a textarea.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not data. It admits only families in its roles. Its scenarios are signing up and managing a plan.
Command suits expert users who jump anywhere by typing, not people who visit now and then. Multi-brand's customers return now and then, and most visits last a few minutes.
Right-click menus suit power users, and people who don't know to right-click never find them. Multi-brand's customers see it fresh each time. Plan actions sit in a visible menu.
Multi-brand draws on core, content and media families, not data. It avoids tools staff use all day and points those to Dense data.
Hover cards need a mouse, and touch screens have no hover. Multi-brand's customers use any device. A popover opens plan details by tap.

answers.question: brand.q1
answers.why: A neutral base each brand can color.

answers.question: brand.q3
answers.why: Each brand brings its own face, Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans or Poppins, on one shared type scale, so brands differ and the system stays one.

considers.readability: All three are screen sans faces with open shapes; the shared scale keeps body size and line height the same in every brand.
considers.legibility: Each brand checks its face's confusable characters in its own data; the scale gives every brand the same sizes to check at.
considers.scalability: All three have a wide range of weights, so every role in the shared scale has a weight in every brand.
considers.numerals: Inter has tabular figures; the brands that show tables lean on it.
considers.scripts: Latin, with accents, in all three; Poppins also covers Devanagari. Other scripts need a face per brand.
considers.recognition: The face is how each brand is known on a shared system.
considers.familiarity: Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans and Poppins are widely seen on the web, so none feels strange.
considers.personality: A neutral base each brand can color: the face carries the brand, the scale stays neutral.
considers.performance: One family per brand: a page loads only its own brand's face.
considers.licensing: SIL Open Font License, all three: free to embed in apps and on the web.
considers.fallback: Each falls back to system-ui, as its tokens say; the shared scale keeps the layout steady while a face loads.

color.$description: Color options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

slate-deep.$description: The slate-deep hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

150.$description: Derived: the step between 100 and 200 on the scheme's step curve (medium-ease), even in contrast. Added so a floating layer sits one step above raised in dark.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.

round.$description: A circle of a square: avatars, radio dots, thumbs and round buttons.

pill.$description: A capsule of any box: tracks, progress, the scroll thumb and pill controls.

size.$description: Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

line-height.$description: Line height options: ratios of the text size. The type scale generates them.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 150ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower speed for larger moves, about 300ms.

standard.$description: A standard ease-out: fast at the start, settling slowly, with no overshoot.

strong-out.$description: A strong ease-out: most of the way in the first third of the time, then a soft stop. For exits.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

card.$description: Raw shadow for card in light mode.

overlay.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in light mode.

overlay-dark.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in dark mode.

1_5.$description: An icon stroke width option, on Lucide's 24px grid.

open-ds.why: A touch target sets the 44px default. Compact is one 8px step below it; large equals the default, as brand color marks the main action. Rows are a decision of their own and stay one control tall.
Comfortable in every brand: panels and fields breathe; rows stay tight.
